slides.text: Since the Sun-God's edict, no citizen of Solaris can lie: whatever sin you commit twists your shadow into the shape of your crime. Thieves drag shadows with twenty grasping fingers; betrayers cast silhouettes with daggers in their teeth. Down in the windowless cellars beneath the weaver's district, I make my living with midnight silk and silver needles, stitching counterfeit shadows onto the heels of the desperate.

Just before dawn, the door to my shop was unbolted by Lord Vane, the High Inquisitor who had burned a hundred of my clients at the stake. I reached for my shears, prepared to die. Instead, he stepped into the circle of my tallow lantern and lifted the hem of his white cloak. The cobblestones behind his boots were completely bare. He had no shadow at all.

'A man whose shadow shows a monster is merely human,' the Inquisitor whispered, his voice trembling as he laid a bag of royal rubies on my cutting table. 'A man with no shadow has nothing left inside him for the light to touch. Sew me a wicked one, tailor—a thief's, a coward's, anything—before the temple realizes their saint has been hollow for ten years.'
